correctness.rationale: For a unit-row projection the conditional squared decrement is e^T A^T diag(p) A e; this sharp one-step objective is concave and invariant under leaf permutations. For common leaf probability q, the radial block in the weighted Gram matrix has trace p_0+cq and determinant (c−ma²)p_0 q, and the contrast eigenvalue is (1−b)q. With alpha=c/m and delta=alpha−a²>0, the characteristic polynomial at lambda_R=delta/(1+alpha+2a) expands to −delta[p_0−(alpha+a)/(1+alpha+2a)]²; at zero of this square lambda_R is the smaller radial eigenvalue. Concavity in a fixed radial covariance basis implies strict increase until its unique maximum. After dividing by q, the determinant at the contrast level is m[t(b−a²)−b(1−b)]. For b≤0 the radial level is always smaller by its diagonal entry c; for 0<b≤a² the determinant is negative; for b>a² it crosses once before or after the radial maximizer. Comparison with t_0 gives the stated switch inequality, and substitution gives the rates and the limiting cases. For an arbitrary optimum, symmetrizing fixes its hub probability, so its Rayleigh quotient on a radial minimizing eigenvector equals rho_* exactly. This entails the full eigenvector equation for the unsymmetrized law; subtraction and invertibility of A force equal weights since a>0 and positive optimal weights ensure both row response types are nonzero. The reasoning holds at the crossing. The supporting script was inspected, not executed; numeric comparisons are not proofs of uniqueness.
